name: Toon outlines and cel shading for a three.js scene
worksWith: billboard-sprites-3d (N-02): sprites use their own unlit material and stay untouched; 3D props and terrain around them get the toon look
any three.js 0.149.0 scene with lit materials (Lambert, Phong, Standard)
oneLiner: One call turns an existing three.js scene cel-shaded: every lit material becomes a toon copy with 2-4 light bands, a cool shadow tint, rim light and hard glints, and every solid mesh gets an inverted-hull ink outline that shares its buffers, keeps a steady screen width and thins out on small or far objects; the game's scene graph, rules and material changes keep working and remove() restores the original materials exactly.
fits: low-poly 3D adventures and tactics games that want a cel-shaded, hand-inked look
an options switch between the game's normal look and a toon look
3D scenes with procedural primitives (boxes, cylinders, icosahedra) whose hard corners need gap-free outlines
notFor: skinned or morph-target characters that need outlines (they get toon shading only)
instanced grass or crowds that need outlines (toon shading only)
scenes built from ShaderMaterial / unlit Basic materials (left unchanged)

needs: one call to toon.update(dtMs) right before every renderer.render (play, pause, title / end, frozen stills)
optional: fade(mesh) when the game fades occluding props with its own shader uniform
provides: GameDNA_Toon3D.create / apply; toon.update / set / setEnabled / remove / optOut
toon.state(), toon.list() (why a mesh has no outline), toon.original(mesh), toon.shellOf(mesh)
checks/toon-checks.py (exact restore, outline per eligible mesh, ring pixels; 4 mutants), checks/host-facing.py (the hosts' facing + feet checks with the addon on)

assets: none: the gradient map is generated in code
hostRequires: a three.js scene: three.js 0.149.0 as window.THREE (scene, camera, renderer)
